key_insight: The paper introduces a new two-point flux for multi-species compressible flow that is both entropy conserving and kinetic energy preserving.
engineering_relevance: This improves the fidelity and robustness of high-order CFD solvers for supersonic and space-flight applications involving mixing chemical species.
method: Adapted Ranocha’s single-species two-point flux methodology to the multi-species case.
Designed the flux to satisfy both entropy conservation and kinetic energy preservation.
Compared against existing multi-species fluxes in benchmark tests.
evidence_signal: The proposed flux was evaluated on density pulse advection and Taylor–Green vortex cases, where it preserved both target properties while prior fluxes preserved only one.
watch_item: The flux is only one component of a full high-order scheme, so implementation details and compatibility with the surrounding discretization still matter.
paper_title: A Kinetic Energy Preserving and Entropy Conserving Two-Point Flux for Multi-species Compressible Flow
